findings.desc: quantum_claim_check only applies the requestedStrength CLI argument to built-in cases. In packages/main/src/handlers/quantum-claim-admissibility.ts:108-110 the handler skips args.requestedStrength whenever evidenceJson or evidencePath is present, even though the command schema exposes requestedStrength as a normal argument and describes unsupported strengths as fail-closed overclaims. As a result, caller-supplied complete evidence plus --requestedStrength=production/theory can be evaluated as advance unless the JSON itself redundantly includes requestedStrength, creating CLI/direct-input policy drift and a fail-closed overclaim bypass. Apply requestedStrength consistently after parsing all evidence sources, or reject combining it with evidenceJson/evidencePath so the command cannot silently ignore the overclaim signal.

docs/requirements/decisions/claim-admissibility-adapter-pack-framework.md says the M2/default registry includes the Quantum local gate-policy projection (lines 292-313), but the actual default Quantum pack remains descriptor/normalization-only with gatePolicies: Object.freeze([]) in packages/main/src/core/claim-admissibility/pack-framework.ts. The M3 projection is registered separately as the quantum_claim_check CLI handler, so the doc can falsely imply the generic adapter framework M4 Gate Policy Adapter is complete. Reword to keep the pack registry at descriptor/normalization only, describe quantum_claim_check as a separate local M3 projection, and update the stale Open Design Question reference to beyond M3 or equivalent.
